_comment: PUBLIC EXAMPLE SUITE. This is not a benchmark and must never be reported as one.
The real suites are withheld (docs/PUBLISHING.md): a published benchmark stops measuring
anything the moment models train on it. This file exists for the opposite reason -- so that
anyone who clones the repo can run smoke.py and the full harness end to end and watch them
work, instead of being asked to take the published numbers on faith.
The task below is deliberately a textbook exercise that every model has already memorised.
That is the point: leaking it teaches models nothing they do not already know, so it costs
nothing to publish, while still exercising every part of the machinery -- multi-turn prompts,
turn-scoped test sections, fragment detection via the entry symbol, reference calibration,
It cannot rank models and must not be used to. Every model worth serving scores 100% here.

turns: Write a `Stack` class in Python with `push(item)`, `pop()`, `peek()` and `__len__()`. `pop()` and `peek()` must raise `IndexError` on an empty stack. Reply with the complete contents of solution.py.

Add a `min()` method that returns the smallest item currently on the stack, and must run in O(1) -- do not scan the stack on each call. It raises `IndexError` when the stack is empty. Keep everything from the previous turn working. Reply with the complete contents of solution.py.

There is a bug: after pushing 5, 3, 5 and then popping once, `min()` returns 5 instead of 3. Fix it, and add an optional `capacity` argument to `__init__` (default `None` = unbounded); when the stack is full, `push()` must raise `OverflowError`. Reply with the complete contents of solution.py.
